t.r: Loess Plateau, northern China (Gansu, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Henan, Ningxia)
t.d: Earth-sheltered cave dwellings dug into loess cliffs or around sunken courtyards.
t.tech: Excavation into loess; arched hoop construction

t.d: Porcelain from the Arita area, where most early Japanese and export porcelain was made.
t.tech: porcelain

t.d: Japan's first porcelain, exported through Imari.
t.tech: underglaze blue with overglaze enamels and gold

t.d: Stoneware, notably purple shidei teapots, teacups and sake vessels.
t.tech: stoneware, tochiri decoration
t.auth: maker's seal; shidei purple colour

t.d: Yokkaichi semi-stoneware with high petalite content, giving flame-resistant donabe and teapots.
t.tech: petalite-rich stoneware fired for thermal shock resistance
t.auth: Yokkaichi-Banko marks; petalite body

t.d: Cut, engraved and painted glass and crystal of Bohemia, prized since the Renaissance.
t.tech: Wheel cutting and engraving, blowing, painting, reverse glass painting
t.mat: Potash-chalk glass; lead crystal in later work
t.auth: Maker's marks of named glassworks; potash-chalk composition in early pieces

t.d: Dutch tin-glazed earthenware painted mainly in cobalt blue.
t.tech: tin glaze with underglaze cobalt
t.auth: 'Delfts Blauw' hand-painted on the base

t.d: Painted tin-glazed earthenware, first Italian centre to use lustre.
t.tech: tin glaze, lustre

t.d: Cut-glass craft of Tokyo with overlay colour glass cut in fine geometric patterns.
t.tech: Coloured overlay blown over clear glass, marked, rough- and fine-cut on wheels, polished
t.mat: Clear or lightly tinted glass with coloured overlay
t.auth: Designated Tokyo Traditional Craft (1985) and National Traditional Craft (2002); traditional patterns such as nanako

t.d: Earthy tea ware with translucent beige glaze whose crazing darkens with use.
t.tech: stoneware with kan-nyū crazing
t.auth: glaze crazing darkened by use

t.d: Affordable everyday porcelain, once Japan's leading blue-and-white producer.
t.tech: underglaze cobalt and celadon
t.auth: sold under the Hasami ware label since 2002

t.d: Porous, coarse-clay Iga stoneware whose heat-retaining body makes it the classic donabe material.
t.tech: wood-fired climbing kilns; glazed interior, porous exterior
t.auth: kiln mark; coarse unglazed exterior; sized in sun

t.d: Korean-derived stoneware prized for tea-ceremony bowls.
t.tech: iron underglaze painting, combined glazes
t.auth: style (e-karatsu, Chōsen, madara)

t.d: French hard-paste porcelain from local kaolin, protected by a geographical indication.
t.tech: hard-paste porcelain, overglaze decoration
t.auth: Porcelaine de Limoges mark only for pieces made and decorated in Haute-Vienne (GI INPI-1702)

t.p: over 1,300 years; tea wares from 16th century
t.d: Stoneware and porcelain making about half of Japanese pottery.
t.tech: glazed stoneware (Shino, Oribe, Ki-Seto, Setoguro)

t.d: Korean earthenware jars, unglazed or dark-brown glazed, used for fermenting and storing kimchi, soy sauce and pastes.
t.tech: Coil-built earthenware fired at 600–700 °C unglazed or over 1100 °C with dark-brown glaze; slightly porous body lets ferments breathe.
t.auth: Hand-thrown body, dark brown glaze, breathable walls; look for size names and workshop marks rather than mass-moulded uniformity.

t.d: Hand-moulded, low-fired, porous tea bowls taken from the kiln while glowing hot.
t.tech: hand shaping, low firing, lead glazes
t.mat: clay, black, red and white glazes
t.auth: attribution to Raku family generation

t.d: Stoneware with thick white glaze, red scorch marks and pinholes.
t.tech: thick white shino glaze
t.auth: glaze texture and scorch

t.d: Making of glazed stoneware mortars with combed kushi-no-me ridges inside, paired with wooden surikogi pestles, for sesame, miso and tororo.
t.tech: Thrown bowl, exterior glazed, interior left unglazed and combed with radiating grooves before firing
t.mat: Stoneware clay, glaze; sansho or other wood pestle
t.auth: Unglazed combed interior in a ceramic body; plastic versions wear quickly and are not traditional.

t.d: Hand-thrown tin-glazed earthenware with six permitted natural colours.
t.tech: wheel-thrown, twice fired, hand-painted
t.auth: Denominación de Origen (1997): certified workshops' hologram and marks

t.d: Stoneware centre best known for red shudei kyusu.
t.tech: stoneware, built-in clay sieves
t.auth: potter's name and clay

t.d: Unglazed purple, red and beige clay teapots made from clay near Lake Tai.
t.tech: hand-built slab construction or slipcasting; high firing without glaze
t.auth: maker's seals, clay colour and texture, hand-built vs slipcast; price depends on age, clay and artist

t.d: Japanese vegetable pickling in salt, brine or a fermented rice-bran bed, using tubs, pressing stones and screw-top pickle presses.
t.tech: Vegetables pressed under weight in salt or buried in a daily-stirred rice-bran (nuka) bed.
t.mat: Wooden or ceramic tubs, enamel or plastic nukadoko containers, pickle presses
t.auth: Traditional nukadoko is kept alive by daily hand-stirring; pressing containers are judged by lid pressure and capacity rather than brand.

t.d: Preparation of very finely ground coffee boiled unfiltered in a cezve, inscribed by UNESCO in 2013.
t.tech: slow heating of coffee and water in a long-handled pot until it foams, served with grounds settling
t.mat: hammered copper or brass, tinned; silver; later steel and ceramic
t.auth: hand-hammered marks, tinned interior, riveted long handle; capacity sized in cups

t.p: Technique established early Edo period; oldest surviving piece 1524
t.d: Japanese lacquerware on wooden cores with an unusually durable layered undercoat.
t.tech: many layers of urushi mixed with powdered diatomaceous earth (ji-no-ko) over wood
t.auth: ji-no-ko undercoat on solid wood; Wajima-style pieces are also made by overseas workshops

t.d: 700-year forged-blade tradition begun by Kyoto swordsmith Chiyozuru Kuniyasu making sickles; designated traditional craft, now centred on Takefu Knife Village.
t.tech: hand forging of agricultural-tool heritage, prized toughness
t.auth: Echizen Uchihamono Cooperative designation; maker mei from Takefu smiths

t.d: Electrolytic silver plating brought to France when Charles Christofle bought the Ruolz and Elkington patents in 1842.
t.tech: electroplating of silver onto nickel-silver or copper blanks
t.auth: Christofle pieces carry the house hallmark and plating-grade numerals; the company publishes a hallmark guide.

t.d: Siliceous shale finishing stones quarried around Kyoto and used since the late 12th century for final sharpening of blades.
t.tech: quarried and hand-cut natural stone, used with water and slurry for finish polishing
t.mat: siliceous shale from the Tamba geological formation
t.auth: natural stone with layered shale grain, free of mineral inclusions; graded by mine and hardness, no uniform synthetic texture

t.r: Laguiole and Thiers, Massif Central, France
t.d: Occitan slipjoint pocket-knife tradition, first designed by Jean-Pierre Calmels in 1829, which added the corkscrew in 1880 for Auvergnat café owners and gave rise to the sommelier knife.
t.tech: forged blade and backspring, hand-fitted slipjoint, decorated spring and forged bee
ctr: Laguiole village (Forge de Laguiole, Honoré Durand)
t.auth: Name is not legally protected; look for named workshop, hand-finished spring and bee, made-in-France marking.

t.d: Japan's oldest carpentry-tool region; chisel and plane-blade steel skills carried into small-volume kitchen knife making.
t.tech: hand forging from carpentry-tool tradition, disciplined geometry and heat treatment
t.auth: Miki maker marks

t.r: Morioka and Mizusawa (Oshu), Iwate prefecture, Japan
t.d: Sand-cast ironware tradition begun with tea-ceremony kettles for the Nambu domain, now covering tetsubin, pots, frying pans and omelette pans.
t.tech: sand-mould casting, hand-finished; arare (hailstone) surface patterns; bare or blackened rust-resistant finish
t.auth: Designated traditional craft; foundry marks of Iwachu/Oigen; fine-grain smooth casting; arare texture on kettles

t.d: Cast ironware from Iwate, best known for tetsubin kettles; designated a national traditional craft in 1975.
t.tech: iron casting, arare surface patterns
t.auth: traditional-craft certification; bare iron interior on true kettles

t.d: Government-designated forged-blade craft: hand-forged, clay-quenched single-bevel knives made under a division of labour between smith, sharpener and handle fitter.
t.tech: forge-welding steel to soft iron at ~900 °C, hand hammering, clay-coated water quench, hand sharpening and finishing
t.mat: carbon steel (shirogami, aogami) on soft iron; magnolia handles with buffalo-horn ferrules
t.auth: Sakai smith and sharpener marks; Tokugawa-era 'gokuin' quality stamp heritage; kasumi/hongasumi finish with urasuki hollow back

t.d: Sword-making city since swordsmith Motoshige settled there; today Japan's volume centre for machine-forged stainless Western-style knives finished by hand.
t.tech: machine stamping/forging and quenching, hand sharpening and handle fitting
t.mat: stainless and powder steels (VG10, VG-MAX, molybdenum-vanadium), Swedish steels
t.auth: 'Seki Japan' marks; Kai, Misono, Masahiro house stamps

t.d: Sheffield has been famous for cutlery since the 17th century; crucible and stainless steel pioneered there, with remaining 'little mester' workshops.
t.tech: forging and grinding, crucible steel, stainless steel
t.mat: carbon and stainless steel, bone, horn and wood scales
t.auth: 'Made in Sheffield' mark and Cutlers' Company registered marks; vintage carvers often bear maker and 'Sheffield England'

t.p: 1624 (Cutlers' Company) – present; Old Sheffield Plate 1740s–1840s; EPNS after 1840
t.d: The English cutlery city: fused silver-on-copper 'Old Sheffield Plate', then electroplated nickel silver, alongside steel knives and canteens.
t.tech: fused plate rolled from silver-clad copper ingots; later electroplating over nickel silver; forged and ground knife blades
t.mat: sterling silver, copper, nickel silver, stainless steel
t.auth: Old Sheffield Plate shows copper 'bleeding' at worn edges and has no hallmark; EPNS is stamped; 'Sheffield' marks are controlled by the Cutlers' Company.

t.d: Germany's 'City of Blades', home to firms making knives, scissors, razors and table cutlery.
t.tech: forged and ground steel blades
t.auth: Solingen-marked steel from the city's firms; look for the maker's stamp alongside 'Solingen'.

t.d: The 'Klingenstadt' tradition of forged swords, knives, scissors and razors behind Wüsthof, Zwilling, Böker, Güde and Herder.
t.tech: drop-forging from a single blank with integral bolster, ice-hardening, hand finishing
t.mat: X50CrMoV15 stainless, carbon steels, POM and wood handles
t.auth: 'Solingen' is a protected origin mark; forged full tang, maker's trident/twins stamps

t.d: French knife capital where about a hundred companies make seventy percent of French kitchen, table and pocket knives, including the Sabatier houses.
t.tech: full forging, water-powered grinding historically, hand assembly
t.mat: carbon and stainless steel, boxwood, olive, ebony, POM
t.auth: 'Sabatier' alone is unprotected; look for registered house marks (K, Elephant, Lion, Diamant) and 'forgé à Thiers'

t.d: France's knife capital on the Durolle river, source of most French cutting tools including laguiole-type and steak knives.
t.tech: forged blades; hand assembly and fitting of handles; polishing
t.mat: stainless and carbon steel, horn, wood, resin
t.auth: Le Thiers model (1993) is a registered town pattern; 'laguiole' alone is not a protected name, so check for a maker's stamp.

t.d: Free-forged working blades from Shikoku's forestry and farming country: axes, sickles, hoes and rustic kurouchi kitchen knives in carbon steel.
t.tech: free forging without moulds, hand hammering, kurouchi finish
t.auth: rustic hand-forged kurouchi finish; Tosa cooperative labelling

t.d: Niigata metalworking district whose artisans hand-polish stainless barware to a mirror finish for Japanese bar brands.
t.tech: hand mirror-polishing of pressed stainless steel
t.auth: Made-in-Japan marking and seamless mirror finish.

t.r: Tsubame and Sanjo, Niigata Prefecture, Japan
t.d: Metalworking region begun with nails and farm hardware; Tsubame excels in precision stainless engineering, Sanjo in traditional hand forging.
t.tech: Tsubame: stamping and precision stainless; Sanjo: hammer forging, nashiji and kurouchi finishes
t.mat: stainless (CROMOVA, VG10), SKD/SLD semi-stainless, shirogami, aogami
t.auth: maker mei; Sanjo forges' hand-ground finishes vs Tsubame machine precision

t.d: Main centre of Russian samovar making; 'Tula samovar' is the city's mark.
t.tech: metalworking
t.auth: 'Tula samovar' brand mark

t.d: Coppersmithing town near Mont-Saint-Michel, source of professional French copper cookware.
t.tech: spun and hammered copper, tin or stainless lining
t.mat: copper, tin, stainless, bronze or cast-iron handles
t.auth: maker stamp; gauge 1.5–2.5 mm

t.d: Norman 'city of copper' whose hammered copper and brass pans gave the town its name; home of Mauviel since 1830.
t.tech: hammering and spinning of copper sheet, tin or stainless lining, riveted iron, bronze or stainless handles
t.auth: Maker stamps (Mauviel 1830), gauge 1.5–2.5 mm, hammered or polished exterior, tin or stainless lining

t.d: Hand-engraved silver and gold buckles made as rodeo prizes and worn as Western dress, now a collecting field.
t.tech: hand engraving, overlay figures, soldered gold trim
t.mat: sterling silver, German silver, gold plate over brass
t.auth: PRCA/NFR award engraving and pre-1970 dates add value; many reproduction 'Tiffany' buckles are fakes

t.d: Cottage and later factory clockmaking around Triberg, Furtwangen, Schonach and Schönwald; home of the cuckoo clock.
t.tech: wooden-plate and brass movements, bellows-and-pipe cuckoo calls, hand carving, painted dials
t.mat: lime and pine wood, brass, cast-iron weights
t.auth: VdS (Black Forest Clock Association) certificate of authenticity: made in the Black Forest with a mechanical movement.

t.d: Provincial French longcase clocks with potbellied cases, made at up to 60,000 a year in 1850–90.
t.tech: iron-framed movements, long ornate pendulums
t.auth: Embossed brass pendulum and pediment, enamel dial signed with the retailer.

t.d: Restoration and Georgian London clockmaking that produced lantern, longcase and bracket clocks and the anchor escapement.
t.tech: anchor escapement, seconds pendulum, fusee spring clocks, repeating work
t.mat: brass, steel, ebony, walnut, oak, lacquer
t.auth: Signed dials ("Londini fecit"), original movement-to-case match, cases by specialist joiners.

t.d: Saxon watch town founded on Ferdinand Adolph Lange's 1845 workshop, nationalised as GUB and revived after 1990.
t.tech: three-quarter plate, hand-engraved balance cocks, double assembly
t.auth: "Glashütte" on the dial requires most value added in the town.

t.d: Swedish cottage industry making Mora longcase clocks, over 50,000 movements in the 19th century.
t.tech: cottage-made movements, painted cases
ctr: Krång Anders Andersson ("A A S Mora")
t.auth: "A A S Mora" dial inscription; regional case shapes.

t.d: Craftsmanship of mechanical watchmaking and art mechanics, inscribed by UNESCO in 2020 as a joint Swiss–French nomination.
t.tech: hand bevelling, pivot making, polishing, dial making and printing, assembly; musical automata
t.auth: Movement signatures and Geneva Seal, Poinçon or observatory certificates; maker archives issue extracts.

t.r: Central Mexico (Puebla, Oaxaca and basalt regions)
t.d: Hand-carving of tripod mortars and tejolote pestles from single blocks of vesicular basalt, continuing Aztec and Maya practice.
t.tech: Chiselled from one block of porous basalt; interior left rough so worn bubbles keep renewing the grinding surface
t.auth: Real basalt is porous, heavy and needs breaking in with rice; concrete imitations are smooth, lighter, shed grit and never season.

t.d: Weaving of elaborate wave-patterned silk for wedding longyi.
t.tech: Silk weaving of wave or houndstooth acheik patterns
t.auth: Silk acheik wave pattern

t.d: Industrial resin-resist printing of batik-inspired cloth for African markets.
t.tech: Resin resist with wooden stamp blocks per colour
t.auth: Maker name, product and design number printed on the selvedge; design equally clear on both faces

t.d: Gold and silver thread embroidery on velvet used for the karakou and kaftan.
t.tech: El Majboud raised metallic-thread embroidery

t.d: Regional traditional dress of the German-speaking Alps: dirndl, lederhosen, Janker, loden.
t.tech: tailoring, embroidery, loden fulling
t.auth: regional cut, colours and embroidery; horn buttons; hand-stitched seams

t.d: Knitted earflap hats in camelid and sheep wool with patterned bands, part of Quechua and Aymara dress.
t.tech: hand knitting in the round with colourwork bands
t.auth: hand-knitted camelid fibre; regional motifs; tassels and earflaps

t.d: Cable-stitch jumper knitting developed on the Aran Islands and exported worldwide from the 1950s.
t.tech: Hand-knit cables, honeycomb, diamond, trellis and moss stitch panels
t.auth: Hand-knit pieces show irregular tension; islands provenance; cream undyed wool

t.d: Akan strip weaving of named-pattern kente, traced by oral tradition to Bonwire.
t.tech: Narrow-strip loom weaving with multiple heddles; strips sewn together
t.auth: Hand-woven strips sewn edge to edge (not printed); kente is a Ghanaian geographical indication

t.d: Horizontal-loom strip weave sewn into broad cloth for agbada and other prestige dress.
t.tech: narrow-band weaving on horizontal loom, strips 4–6 in wide sewn edge to edge
t.mat: cotton, wild silk; indigo and red dyes
t.auth: strip seams visible; named weaves alari (red silk), sanyan (beige silk), etu (indigo cotton)

t.d: Silk brocade weaving with gold and silver zari, the source of Banarasi saris and dupattas.
t.tech: Handloom brocade with supplementary zari weft; jangla, tanchoi, cutwork, tissue, butidar designs
t.mat: Katan silk, kora organza, georgette, zari
ctr: Varanasi weaver families; Banaras Brocades and Saris GI association
t.auth: GI tag; pure silk and tested zari; reverse shows floating threads of hand brocade

t.r: Kutch and Saurashtra, Gujarat; Rajasthan, India
t.d: Fingernail-tied resist dyeing by the Khatri community producing thousands of tiny dots.
t.tech: Bheendi knot tying; mothra, ekdali, shikari tying patterns
ctr: Khatri community of Kutch and Saurashtra; Jamnagar
t.auth: Raised puckered dots that remain after untying; hand-tied irregularity

t.d: Woollen blankets worn as cloaks by Sotho people, with named designs marking rank, marriage and initiation.
t.tech: mill-woven wool or wool/dralon blankets with pin-stripe worn vertically
t.auth: Aranda label, correct named design and colourway, pin-stripe orientation

t.d: Men's ceremonial cloak worn over the thobe for weddings, prayers and national events.
t.tech: hand-finished woven cloak
t.auth: natural camel hair or wool, hand finishing

t.d: French labourers' blue work clothing — moleskin or drill jackets and trousers — now reproduced by heritage makers.
t.tech: Cut-and-sewn heavy cotton, patch pockets, button cuffs
t.mat: Cotton moleskin, drill, twill, denim in hydrone blue
t.auth: Thick cotton moleskin or drill, hydrone-blue dye that fades with wear, made-in-France labels and simple unlined construction.

t.d: Malian cotton cloth patterned with fermented mud.
t.tech: Mud-dye painting on strip-woven cotton

t.d: Long hooded cloak of coarse wool, white for men of rank, worn for weddings and holidays.
t.tech: woven wool with pointed hood
t.auth: hand-woven wool, pointed hood

t.d: Felted wool beret making around Oloron-Sainte-Marie, industrialised in the 19th century.
t.tech: knitted then felted and shaped wool

t.d: Silk and half-silk ikat with bold patterns from the Silk Road oases.
t.tech: Warp ikat (abrband)

t.d: Sheer lightweight silk and cotton weaving with small butis.
t.tech: Handloom with extra-weft buti motifs
t.auth: Transparent lightweight hand; hand-woven buti

t.d: Tzotzil and Tzeltal women's backstrap-loom brocade identifying community through motif and colour.
t.tech: Backstrap loom, supplementary-weft brocade, embroidery
t.auth: Hand-brocaded designs, selvedge panels joined by stitching, community-specific patterns

t.d: White-on-white hand embroidery of Lucknow used on kurtas, saris and dupattas.
t.tech: Hand embroidery in many named stitches on light cloth
t.auth: Hand-stitch irregularity; shadow-work on reverse

t.d: Coast Salish hand-knitting of heavy shawl-collar sweaters in undyed wool with pictorial motifs.
t.tech: Hand-spun bulky single-ply, hand-knit, motifs worked in natural shades
t.mat: Undyed white, grey and brown wool
t.auth: Hand-spun undyed wool, knitted by Coast Salish knitters; Cowichan Tribes trademark; imitations (Mary Maxim, Pendleton, HBC) are 'Cowichan-style'

t.d: Flecked woollen tweed from Donegal, originally handwoven and since the 1950s–60s mostly machine woven, used for caps, suits and coats.
t.tech: plain and herringbone weave with coloured neps spun into the yarn
t.auth: irregular coloured flecks in the yarn; mill or handweaver label; made in Donegal

t.d: Flecked Irish tweed, hand-woven until the 1950s–60s.
t.tech: Hand and power-loom weaving

t.d: Sámi handicraft of clothing, knives, cups and bags, with the gákti its most important garment.
t.tech: sewing, pewter embroidery, leather and root work
t.mat: reindeer skin, wool, velvet, silk, pewter thread
t.auth: red, green, blue, yellow palette; regional band patterns; made by Sámi makers

t.d: Hand-weaving of hats from toquilla palm fibre, inscribed by UNESCO in 2012.
t.tech: fibre boiled, sulphur-bleached and hand-woven from crown to brim; finished by washing, moulding and pressing
t.auth: weave count (carreras) and evenness; Montecristi and Pile superfinos are finest

t.d: Hand-woven cotton cloth used for netela, kuta and gabi shawls and the habesha kemis.
t.tech: handloom weaving, embroidered borders
t.auth: hand-woven cotton; layer count distinguishes netela (1), kuta (2), gabi (4)

t.d: Ewe strip weaving with double-woven bands.
t.tech: Double-woven strip weaving
t.auth: Hand-woven double bands

t.d: Stranded colourwork using two colours per row in a limited palette, made fashionable in 1921.
t.tech: Stranded knitting in the round, short floats, OXO and star bands
t.auth: Only two colours per round, Shetland wool, traditional motif bands; 'Fair Isle' properly means Shetland patterns, not any stranded knit

t.d: Hand-spun cotton strip cloth, revived as a national symbol.
t.tech: Women spin and dye; narrow strips woven on horizontal looms and sewn together
t.auth: Official authenticity label since 2021

t.r: Channel Islands and British fishing coasts
t.d: Seaman's jumper knitting from Guernsey, spread to Cornish, Yorkshire and Scottish fishing villages with local patterns.
t.tech: Tight knitting in the round, underarm gusset, split welt, village-specific textured patterns
t.auth: Diamond underarm gusset, shoulder strap and rope-ladder ribbing; hand-finishing on Guernsey

t.d: Hardangersøm whitework used on bunad aprons, belts and blouses.
t.tech: counted-thread cutwork
t.auth: geometric kloster blocks and cut squares in white on white

t.d: Home-woven island tweed protected by statute.
t.tech: Hand weaving at weavers' homes; dyeing, spinning and finishing on the islands
t.auth: Orb certification mark stamped on the cloth; definition under the Harris Tweed Act 1993

t.d: Hand-making of men's cloaks of camel hair and wool with zari edging; bisht skills UNESCO-listed 2025.
t.tech: Hand weaving and sewing; gold or silver zari edge embroidery
t.mat: Camel hair, goat wool, wool, linen; gold and silver thread
t.auth: Hand-made Hasawi pieces with pure gold-thread trim rank highest.

t.d: Hand-embroidered geometric motifs on strip-woven babban riga robes of the Hausa aristocracy.
t.tech: hand embroidery in silk or cotton on stitched cotton panels
t.auth: aska biyu 'two knives' triangles on front left, spiral motifs at back; strip-cloth construction

t.d: Loom-woven cotton keffiyehs with fishnet and olive-leaf motifs, kept alive by the Hirbawi factory as imports displaced local weaving.
t.tech: mechanised loom weaving of patterned cotton
t.auth: Hirbawi label; woven not printed pattern; made in Hebron

t.d: Tartan-based dress of the Highlands and Isles: belted plaid, kilt, sporran, plaid.
t.tech: twill weaving of tartan setts, hand pleating
t.auth: sett recorded in the Scottish Register of Tartans; hand-sewn pleats to sett or stripe

t.n: Hong Kong and Shanghai qipao tailoring
t.d: Bespoke cheongsam making that fused Chinese robes with Western darts and fitting, now kept by a few master tailors.
t.tech: Hand-sewing, curved cuts and darts, hand-knotted pankou fastenings and piping
t.auth: Hand-finished seams and frog fastenings, multiple fittings, several days to weeks of work.

t.d: Yoke-patterned sweaters in unspun lopi wool that became a national symbol after 1944 independence.
t.tech: Seamless circular knitting, patterned yoke shaped by decreases
t.auth: Icelandic wool, hand-knit in Iceland; unspun lopi yarn with airy hand

t.d: Single and double ikat saris and cloth of India.
t.tech: Warp, weft and double ikat
t.auth: Pattern visible equally on both faces with slight blurring at motif edges

t.d: Wax-resist dyeing with symbolic motifs that mark life events from birth to burial.
t.tech: Hot wax drawn with canting (tulis) or stamped with copper cap, repeated dyeing
t.mat: Cotton, silk, wax, vegetable and synthetic dyes
t.auth: Batik tulis allows very fine hand-drawn detail; batik cap repeats stamped units with less detail

t.d: Fine muslin weaving with motifs added by discontinuous supplementary weft.
t.tech: Supplementary-weft handloom weaving on cotton muslin
t.auth: Hand-inlaid motifs with no floats on the reverse; very fine cotton count

t.d: Shuttle-loom selvedge denim and faithfully reproduced mid-century jeans from the Sanbi textile region.
t.tech: rope-dyed indigo warp woven on vintage shuttle looms; unsanforized or one-wash finishing; chain-stitch hems
t.mat: long-staple cotton (Zimbabwe, US), natural and synthetic indigo
ctr: Osaka Five: Studio D'Artisan, Denime, Evisu, Full Count, Warehouse
t.auth: selvedge ID line at outseam, mill and house hardware, leather or paper patch, slubby uneven fade

t.d: Kanazawa yūzen dyeing with lifelike natural scenes in gentle gradients, more naturalistic than Kyō-yūzen.
t.tech: Paste-resist yūzen dyeing with realistic motifs such as insect-nibbled leaves
t.auth: Realistic flora with worm-eaten leaf details and soft shading rather than Kyoto's framed, gilded pictures.

t.d: Mulberry-silk sari weaving with contrast korvai borders and temple, check and butta designs.
t.tech: Three-shuttle handloom weaving; korvai interlocked border
t.mat: Pure mulberry silk, South Indian zari
t.auth: GI tag; heavy silk; interlocked border join visible; zari purity test

t.d: Kerala handloom with fine gold or silver thread borders on off-white cotton.
t.tech: Handloom with zari border weaving
